root_idea.summary: The root is organized around two related principles: cutting or severing, and gathering or enclosing.
root_idea.development: Cutting develops into removal, extirpation, and metaphorical overcoming; gathering or enclosing appears in garments, receptacles, accumulated substances, and related object names. The Quranic جُبّ belongs to the well vocabulary.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic noun is displayed under the normalized citation form جُبّ.

senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic account of Joseph, the noun denotes the well into which Joseph is cast. The Quran-focused lexical explanation specifies a well that has not been lined or paved with masonry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut, cut off, or extirpate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may be used generally for cutting something off entirely, including the hump of a camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To castrate or emasculate; to cut off the genitals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use referring to complete removal of the penis, testicles, or genitals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pollinate palm trees with pollen from the male tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agricultural use; the associated season is called the time of جِبَاب or جَبَاب.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To surpass or overcome people in a contest of merit, beauty, honor, or similar distinction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb can describe one person surpassing others, especially in beauty or grounds for esteem.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have or produce a horse marking in which the whiteness of the legs rises toward the knees and hocks.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of the extent of تَحْجِيل, the white marking on a horse's lower legs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To shrink from, be averse to, withdraw from, or relinquish something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The withdrawal may be outward or inward; the construction can describe abandoning obedience or an undertaking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To flee.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a more specific use of withdrawing or going away from something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To satisfy the earth or cattle with water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use referring to supplying water to the earth or to livestock.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Vying or contending for superiority in beauty, honor, lineage, hospitality, or similar qualities.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related verb describes one person competing with another and prevailing; the extension to food is reported but qualified in the lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel's milk, to produce جُبَاب, the substance that gathers like butter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized verbal use concerning the formation of the camel-milk product called جُبَاب.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put on a جُبَّة, a garment or tunic.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is denominal, formed from the garment name جُبَّة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deal or trade in جَبَاجِب, the plural of جُبْجُبَة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized commercial use referring to the containers or tripe called جُبْجُبَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prepare a جُبْجُبَة, or to put preserved meat into one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The preparation concerns a stomach or skin receptacle used for provisions; the preserved meat is called خَلْع in the cited explanation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A well dug for planting a grapevine or similar shoot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agricultural type of well.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The interior shaft or inside of a well, from bottom to top.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This denotes the well's internal extent, whether or not it is lined.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The hollowed stone or basin at the mouth of a well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized architectural sense referring to a stone receptacle or parapet-like structure at the well opening.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A leather bag or sewn hide vessel used for preparing a fermented beverage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A traditional container made by sewing one part of a hide to another; its use is mentioned in connection with a prohibition on such vessels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The spathe or envelope surrounding the flowers of a palm tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may be exchanged with جُفّ in this sense; it is explained through the enclosing interior of the palm inflorescence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A garment, coat, or tunic; also a coat of mail or other defensive coat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The garment may be cut and sewn, quilted, woollen, or used as protective clothing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A receiving, enclosing, or joint-like part: the socket of a spearhead, the part of a horn containing its core, the bony enclosure of the eye, or a receiving joint or junction in a horse's limb or hoof.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sense covers several specialized anatomical and implement terms united by the notion of a part receiving or enclosing another part.

other_classical_meanings.definition: White hair or marking on the lower part of a horse's leg extending toward the hoof.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized equine-color term concerning whiteness around the lower leg and hoof.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The cutting off, cutting into, or erosion of a camel's hump.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can describe either deliberate removal or erosion caused by a saddle so that the hump does not grow large.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The butter-like substance that gathers on the surface of camel milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the coagulated or collected product of camel milk, distinguished from ordinary زُبْد made from cow, sheep, or goat milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Earth or ground, especially hard, rugged, rocky, or cloddy ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may denote the surface of the earth generally, rough land, or lumps and clods of tough clay or mud.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A burial ground or cemetery.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This use is connected lexically with the earth or ground in which burial takes place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seller of جِبَاب, plural garments or coats.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nisbah-like occupational designation derived from جُبَّة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The stomach or tripe of a ruminant animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may serve as a receptacle in which preserved meat, melted fat, or provisions are placed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rounded skin vessel or receptacle for water, preserved meat, grease, or other preparations.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Uses include giving water to camels and macerating colocynth; a camel-side skin could also be fashioned for preparing lasting provisions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small basket or carrier made of skins for removing dust or earth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural جَبَاجِب is used for such skin baskets.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A drum.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural جَبَاجِب occurs in expressions about drums being beaten.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seller of tripe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An occupational designation derived from جُبْجُبَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Food prepared with tripe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A culinary derivative associated with the tripe sense of جُبْجُبَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, having its hump cut off, eroded, or absent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form is جَبَّاءُ; the description can refer to deliberate removal or loss of the hump's prominence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a woman, lacking prominent buttocks or breasts, or having lean thighs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are explicitly reported feminine applications of the adjective and are not general restrictions on the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The female pudendum.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical noun use reported as equivalent to الفرج.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The middle or main part of a road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word denotes the beaten or central course of a road.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse whose leg whiteness rises toward the knees and hocks or reaches the hairs around the hoof.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The exact extent of the white marking varies among the cited descriptions, but the term belongs to equine leg coloration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a well, having a wider, cupola-like hollow in its middle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of the well's internal shape.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having the genitals, testicles, or penis cut off or extirpated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial description of complete castration or emasculation.

cautions: The two Quran occurrences are inflected genitive forms جُبِّ; the public headword is normalized to the citation form جُبّ.

Classical sources record several physical descriptions of a جُبّ; the Quran-focused interpretation specifically identifies the Yusuf passage as an unlined well without making that specification universal.
The broader Classical meanings include several derived forms and homonymous object names; they are kept separate from the Quranic well sense.
